title.narrative: Supporting Lebanese Agriculture stakeholders to Pilot National Good Agriculture Practices (N-GAP)

description.narrative: Lebanon has been struggling with a web of economic and political crises that rapidly worsened since late 2019 and led to raging unemployment and hyperinflation. Lebanon's limited internal production capacity and focus on services sector results in a heavy reliance on imports for products.Agriculture, forestry and fishing make a limited contribution to Lebanon's gross domestic product (GDP) but employ 20-25% of the active labour force and contribute around 17% of total exports. During recent decades, the Lebanese government never made agriculture a priority. As a result, the sector received on average less than 1% of overall government spending. Meanwhile, Lebanon relies for 80% on food imports.The Netherlands embassy in Beirut, amongst others, made substantial investments in the Lebanese agricultural sector during recent years, with programs focusing on various food value chains. A recent agro-food sector analysis highlighted the implementation of National-Good Agricultural Practices (N-GAP) for high potential crops as a key intervention to address issues of low prices for Lebanese agricultural produce in its domestic market. N-GAP would prepare farmers to increase quality and traceability and eventually income by jointly accessing regional markets.This project serves to pilot a national certification and traceability system that helps producers, institutions and main stakeholders improve the efficiency and competitiveness of domestic production in a sustainable way.
